liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jack Straw** (3 reviews): Closes the first set in fine form; Lesh ends the jam with huge, deep bass bombs [12][13][18]
- **Jack-A-Roe** (2 reviews): Played with fire, and Jerry's guitar tone is top-notch; Has a solid groove [12][16]
- **Candyman** (1 review): Cited as evidence that Jerry comes very close to nailing each song [22]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Reviewer calls this the best version ever; Bobby sings with unmatched passion and Jerry answers with sweet licks [12]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): The Terrapin leading into Playin' is very mellow [14]
- **Playin' in the Band** (1 review): Blasts out of Terrapin into cosmic territory, with Brent adding freaked-out synth textures [14]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): A killer version that lands you back on solid ground after the Playin' space [14]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-11-06.150953.sbd.newhouse.miller.flac2496** (recommended): soundboard; 19 songs; 158 min [1]
- **gd79-11-06.sbd.miller.29735.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 155 min; rated 5/5 by 5 [2]. Said about its sound: Sound and mix are extremely good, judged better than the other source [22]
- **gd79-11-06.sbd.clugston.2417.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 156 min; rated 4.19/5 by 21 [4]. Said about its sound: Soundboard quality is excellent, and the reviewer recommends boosting the bass [13]
- **gd1979-11-06.151467.sbd.cm.newhouse.miller.t.flac16**: soundboard; 18 songs; 158 min [7]

## Around the show

- Fall 1979 was a hot stretch; Brent's B3, synth and piano refreshed the band, and this is the reviewer's most replayed show [15]
- Along with 5/9/79, this Jack Straw is ranked the best ever [16]
- Reviewer credits the era's lineup, with Brent and fully matured double drumming, over the earlier Keith and Donna sound [16]
- Suggests hearing Jack Straw from Chicago, 8/20/80, before declaring this show the best [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-11-06.150953.sbd.newhouse.miller.flac2496**: taped by Elliot Newhouse; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 25, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550/TDK-SA90) [1]. Also: Made from Elliot Newhouse's cassette masters, with a Rob Eaton patch source and Joe B. Jones's pitch correction settings [1]
- **gd79-11-06.sbd.miller.29735.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Soundboard to cassette master (Sony TCD5M, UDXL-II tape), then DAT on Panasonic SV3800 at 48k; transferred and edited by Charlie Miller [2]
- **gd79-11-06.sbd.clugston.2417.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [4]
- **gd1979-11-06.151467.sbd.cm.newhouse.miller.t.flac16**: taped by Elliot Newhouse; transferred by All Transfers and Mastering by Charlie Miller  November 25, 2020; source: SBD > Cassette Master (Nakamichi 550/TDK-SA90) [7]. Also: Newhouse cassette masters with Rob Eaton patch and Joe B. Jones pitch settings; 24-bit source 150953 converted to 16-bit, 44.1k [7]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Music on TIDAL: [Grateful Dead - Road Trips Vol. 1 No. 1: New Haven Coliseum, New Haven, CT 10/25/79 / The Spectrum, Philadelphia, PA 11/](https://tidal.com/album/24742054) [24]
